facts.raw_span: A 46-year-old Japanese woman
history of epilepsy
redness and swelling of the right breast
erythema and swelling in the lower right breast
Ultrasound revealed a 54 × 41 × 31 mm low-echo mass with partially unclear margins in the outer right breast
invasive ductal carcinoma (no special type), high grade, ER+, PgR–, HER2 3+, Ki67 70%
Whole-body PET-CT revealed increased uptake in the right axilla, anterior mediastinum, left pleura, and liver
consistent with cT4dN3M1 stage IV breast cancer
lesions nearly disappeared
clinical complete response maintained for 23 months
persistent headache
a 30-mm mass lesion in the right temporal lobe

concepts.why: The patient has a history of invasive ductal carcinoma, which is a type of breast cancer, as indicated by fact F06 and confirmed by fact F08.
The patient's cancer has been classified as stage IV, as indicated by fact F08.
The patient has developed a mass lesion in the right temporal lobe, which is likely a metastasis from the breast cancer, as indicated by fact F12.
The patient has a history of epilepsy, as indicated by fact F02.

rationales.F02: Epilepsy is a separate condition from the breast cancer and its treatment, but the patient's history of epilepsy could be relevant to the new onset of headache and the discovery of a brain mass.
rationales.F06: The biopsy results confirm the diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma.
rationales.F07: The PET-CT scan shows increased uptake in multiple areas, consistent with stage IV breast cancer.
rationales.F08: The diagnosis of stage IV breast cancer is based on the PET-CT scan and other clinical findings.
rationales.F12: The mass lesion in the right temporal lobe is likely a brain metastasis from the breast cancer.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of stage IV breast cancer and the recent development of a mass lesion in the right temporal lobe, as shown by CT and MRI of the head, strongly support the diagnosis of brain metastasis, which explains the patient's persistent headache.
